facts.text: West Bromwich’s football club, founded in 1878 by workers from George Saltar’s Spring Works, is one of the town’s oldest sporting institutions.
The town’s Grand Organ, built in 1862, sits in the historic St Paul’s Church and is prized for its musical and technical qualities.
Oak House, a 16th‑century building in Greets Green, now serves as a museum that showcases the town’s industrial heritage.
West Bromwich railway station opened in 1854 on the Great Western line, linking the town to Birmingham and Wolverhampton.
Legendary rock frontman Robert Plant, born in 1948, grew up in West Bromwich before leading Led Zeppelin to global fame.
The town’s annual West Bromwich Festival features drones, lanterns and Caribbean food, celebrating its diverse community.
